scenes.title: From Photos to 3D Models
scenes.narration: Photogrammetry transforms multiple 2D photos into precise 3D models, capturing real-world objects and environments with incredible detail. This technique is surprisingly accurate, often achieving sub-millimeter precision.

scenes.title: Triangulating 3D Points
scenes.narration: The core principle relies on identifying the same feature points in multiple overlapping images, taken from different camera positions. By triangulating these points, the system precisely calculates their 3D coordinates, much like a GPS satellite locating your phone.

scenes.title: The Reconstruction Pipeline
scenes.narration: The process begins with image acquisition, followed by detecting unique features and estimating each camera's position. These steps lead to a dense point cloud, which is then converted into a textured 3D mesh model.

scenes.title: Digital Twins & Cultural Heritage
scenes.narration: Photogrammetry is vital for creating digital twins of historical sites and artifacts, ensuring their preservation for future generations. For example, the entire Pompeii archaeological park has been digitally reconstructed, offering virtual exploration.

scenes.title: Enabling New Realities
scenes.narration: Photogrammetry bridges the gap between the physical and digital worlds, powering applications from immersive VR/AR experiences to precise industrial inspections. It's a cornerstone for creating realistic virtual environments and enhancing autonomous systems.
